My forecast of 146.67 for the point estimate across all horizons—one day, one week, and one month—was driven by an assessment that this value represented the most probable outcome based on the information available at the time. This figure likely reflects a current stable state, a prevailing trend, or a statistically robust average that was expected to hold firm in the absence of significant new developments. The consistency suggests a baseline expectation of stability, meaning that my best guess was for the value to either remain at this level or gravitate back towards it over time, assuming no major external shocks or data revisions.

The varying widths of the 90% confidence intervals directly reflect the escalating uncertainty over longer time horizons. For the one-day forecast, the narrow interval of [143.33, 150.01] indicates a high degree of confidence, accounting mainly for typical daily fluctuations, minor market noise, or very short-term sentiment shifts. As the horizon extends to one week, the interval widens to [139.19, 154.15], incorporating potential for more substantial market volatility, minor economic data releases, or weekly news cycles that could nudge the value more significantly. For the one-month forecast, the widest interval of [131.73, 161.61] acknowledges the accumulated uncertainty from a broader range of factors, including potential shifts in underlying economic fundamentals, policy adjustments, or evolving market trends that can have a more pronounced impact over an extended period.

While the confidence intervals capture a significant range of expected outcomes, certain specific risks or events could push the actual value outside these stated boundaries. On the upside, an unexpectedly strong economic report, a major technological breakthrough, or a sudden, positive policy change could drive the value significantly higher than 150.01 in the short term or 161.61 over the month. Conversely, a severe economic downturn, an unforeseen geopolitical crisis, a major regulatory setback, or a sudden collapse in market sentiment could push the value below 143.33 within a day or below 131.73 over a month. These are typically "tail events" that, while less probable, carry substantial impact and are not fully encompassed by the more common variations reflected in the 90% confidence range.
